exposure: Fixed number of ITNs allocation strategy
Registration method (counting usual sleeping spaces vs. number of household members)
outcome: Proportion of households having received a net from the campaign
Proportion of households with one net for every two people (enough ITNs)
cohort: The study included 13,901 households across 14 campaigns in Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, South Sudan, and Uganda.
finding: Household registration rates were the most important determinant for receiving campaign nets, and universal coverage campaigns, particularly those using a sleeping space allocation strategy, were more effective in increasing the proportion of households with enough ITNs.
country: Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, South Sudan, Uganda
cross-section timing: Three to 16 months after ITN distribution
